standard_prerequisites.name: The map g
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a structure M satisfying Robinson arithmetic whose domain consists of the values of the numerals, g is the function from the standard numbers to the domain sending n to the value of the numeral n.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted statement names g, and the proof compares g with an arbitrary isomorphism pointwise (1329-1333).

standard_prerequisites.name: Isomorphism of structures
standard_prerequisites.statement: An isomorphism is a bijection between the domains that preserves the interpretations of the constant, the successor, addition, multiplication and the order relation.
standard_prerequisites.use: The step of the induction uses that h commutes with the successor function, h of the successor of n equals the successor of h(n) (1343).

standard_prerequisites.name: Values of terms and numerals
standard_prerequisites.statement: The value of the numeral n+1 in M is the value of the term obtained by applying the successor symbol to the numeral n, hence is the successor in M of the value of the numeral n.
standard_prerequisites.use: The middle of the chain of identities rewrites the value of the numeral n+1 as the successor of the value of the numeral n (1337-1341).

core_obligations: Let h be an isomorphism from the standard model to M and show that g equals h by induction on the natural numbers (1329-1330).
Base case: g(0) is the interpretation of the constant 0 by the definition of g, and h(0) is the same interpretation because h is an isomorphism, so g(0) equals h(0) (1331-1333).
Step: write g(n+1) as the value of the numeral n+1, rewrite it as the value of the successor of the numeral n, and evaluate that as the successor in M of the value of the numeral n (1337-1341).
Identify that last term with the successor of g(n) by the definition of g, then with the successor of h(n) by the induction hypothesis (1341-1342).
Use that h preserves the successor function to rewrite the successor of h(n) as h of the successor of n, which is h(n+1), completing the induction and showing g equals h (1343-1345).
Conclude that every isomorphism from the standard model to M coincides with g, so g is the only one (1345-1346).

proof_roadmap.step: Take an arbitrary isomorphism h and settle the base case of the induction.
Compute g(n+1) through the value of the numeral n+1.
Use the induction hypothesis and the homomorphism property of h to finish the step.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's proposition at source lines 1323-1326: if M is standard then the map g of the preceeding proposition is the only isomorphism from the standard model to M. The 19-line proof (1328-1346) takes an arbitrary isomorphism h and shows g equals h by induction on n: the base case compares g(0) and h(0) through the interpretation of the constant, and the step computes both sides of a seven-term chain of identities g(n+1) = the value of the numeral n+1 = the successor of the value of the numeral n = the successor of g(n) = the successor of h(n) = h(successor of n) = h(n+1), using the induction hypothesis and the homomorphism property of h (1335-1345). The statement records neither the induction nor the chain, and the map g is defined in the preceeding proposition, which is retained as context.
